markdown_report:
The best first experiment is **content-conditioned forgetting inside the existing GRU4Rec**. This targets stale-interest revival and weak alignment with recent activity while retaining one jointly trained model per category. Improvement remains a hypothesis.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users distinguish current usefulness from broad relevance. Recent coherent interactions therefore provide a more defensible intent signal than historical membership alone. (2) Electronics has a 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin and 9.7% negative-beats-positive rate. These measured failures motivate improving contextual discrimination, but do not establish poor validation HR@10. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply mean cosine similarities near zero. Global embedding diversification consequently lacks diagnostic support.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [TLSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04760) motivates learned temporal gating. Historical gaps may identify preference changes, although inactivity does not prove changed intent. (2) [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) motivates sharing information through item text. Its pretrained Transformer results do not establish benefits for a small randomly initialized encoder. (3) [GRU4Rec](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec) motivates BPR-max and multiple negatives. Conservative negative emphasis could address weak margins, but unseen items may be false negatives.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Memory control addresses stale intent; representation sharing addresses sparse identity; objective design addresses confusing rankings. All operate within one GRU network.

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; difficulty 10 means hardest. Each cell gives a positive and negative assessment.

| Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Content-conditioned forgetting | 5: conditional integration / established gates | 7: adaptive memory / uncertain transfer | 8: stale and weak recent fit / no compatibility guarantee | 6: context separation / indirect margin effect | 4: small gate / padding and temporal plumbing |
| Shared trainable title encoder | 4: task adaptation / familiar fusion | 7: sparse transfer / limited text supervision | 7: identifiable connections / lexical shortcuts | 5: sparse discrimination / sparsity unmeasured | 6: compact encoder / vocabulary pipeline |
| Regularized BPR-max | 2: established / little novelty | 7: direct ranking / false negatives | 4: stronger distinctions / no intent mechanism | 9: targets weak margins / sampled proxy | 3: existing objective / careful masking |

**Selected experiment.** At each observed interaction, use its embedding, previous hidden state, and historical inter-event gap to predict coordinate-wise retention. Attenuate memory before the ordinary GRU update. Initialize retention near one; content conditioning lets persistent interests survive long gaps.

This explicitly targets older-interest revival and broadly related items displacing recent-intent matches. Better contextual states may also reduce Electronics’ weak-margin cases; neither effect is established yet.

Compare ordinary GRU, gap-only attenuation, and content-conditioned attenuation sequentially using fixed macro validation HR@10. Keep all four routes, seeds 0/42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Update predictor serialization and preserve diagnostic interfaces. Skip padding updates, read the final nonpadding position, and use no future timestamps. Do not infer unavailable compatibility or review attributes.

idea.description: Add a small content-conditioned retention gate before each recurrent update of the corrected GRU4Rec. Here content means the jointly learned item-ID representation, so this first experiment requires no text encoder, external weights, or additional metadata. Each category retains exactly one jointly trained network and one selected checkpoint.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale-interest revival and insufficient focus on recent coherent activity. Conditional memory attenuation directly targets both mechanisms. Electronics’ weak lower-tail margins provide a model-facing target, although contextual forgetting is an indirect intervention and must demonstrate value through validation.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve the supplied backbone, loss, sampler and optimizer for the first comparison so the retention mechanism is identifiable. Normalize log1p historical gaps using training histories only; supply a missing-gap indicator and neutral gap value when timestamps are unavailable. Never use the time of the prediction target. Initialize gate bias positively and gate weights near zero, and include a near-identity setting in validation. Padding must leave hidden state unchanged and produce masked diagnostic features. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items); if the host contract supplies only item IDs, use one deterministic history-to-gap lookup shared by training and inference, or restrict the implementation to content-conditioned retention when gaps cannot be recovered unambiguously. Do not change the contract silently. Read the largest valid sequence index, never length minus one for left padding. Serialize architecture configuration, timestamp preprocessing state if used, and the selected model state into each category checkpoint; embed the identical architecture in the predictor writer. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), reporting measured margins and their definitions without unavailable category metadata. Select by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, not sampled diagnostic margins. No test access, score fusion, checkpoint averaging, or other-trial checkpoint reuse.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category independently:
  initialize corrected GRU4Rec and retention gate with seed 42
  for epoch in range(at_most_200):
    for batch in range(200):
      h = zeros
      for observed position t in chronological order:
        valid = sequence[:, t] != 0
        x = item_emb(sequence[:, t])
        g = normalized_log_observed_gap(t)  # optional; never next-event time
        retain = sigmoid(Wx(x) + Wh(h) + Wg(g) + bias)
        proposed_h = baseline_GRU_update(x, retain * h)
        h = where(valid, proposed_h, h)
        features[:, t] = where(valid, h, 0)
      loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
      optimize_all_parameters_jointly(loss)
    evaluate_with_fixed_validation_protocol()
  save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor_configuration()
At inference:
  reconstruct identical causal recurrence
  select features at maximum nonpadding index
  score candidates with the model's existing learned scoring function

originality.positive: A minimal conditional retention mechanism connects observed intent drift to the required GRU backbone.
originality.negative: Temporal gates and content-conditioned recurrent updates are established ideas; novelty is limited to the constrained adaptation.

future_potential.positive: The experiment can clarify when a recurrent recommender should preserve persistent preferences versus forget stale activity.
future_potential.negative: Interaction gaps and item embeddings may not identify user purpose, ownership redundancy, or actual equipment compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The core mechanism adds only small trainable projections to one GRU.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal timestamp access, padding behavior, diagnostic compatibility, and exact predictor reconstruction require careful integration.

related_work.title: TLSRec (2022)
contributions: Motivates neural temporal gating between long- and short-term preferences.
limitations: Does not establish improvements under the supplied Amazon GRU4Rec protocol.
Elapsed time alone does not establish changed user intent.

related_work.title: Recformer (KDD 2023)
contributions: Supports item-text representation learning for sparse and cold-start recommendation.
limitations: Uses a pretrained Transformer outside the required backbone.
Its results do not establish gains for a randomly initialized compact text encoder.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec
contributions: Provides recurrent recommendation methods and practical BPR-max and sampled-cross-entropy objectives.
limitations: Objective recommendations require validation under the fixed candidate protocol.
Hard negative emphasis may amplify false-negative supervision.
